Common Items in That Could Become Projectiles During a Hurricane

Did you know there are many items in your community that could become projectiles during a hurricane? Read here to learn more.
Jul 20, 2023 | 3 min read

Living in an association-governed community brings numerous benefits, such as shared amenities, organized maintenance, and a sense of community. However, it's important to be aware of potential hazards that can arise during extreme weather events like hurricanes.

While hurricanes are unpredictable and powerful, there are steps we can take to minimize the risks. In this blog post, we will discuss common items found in association-governed communities that could become projectiles during a hurricane.

By identifying and securing these items, we can help protect our community and ensure the safety of our neighbors.

Patio Furniture and Decorations

One of the most common items in association-governed communities that can become projectiles during a hurricane is patio furniture and decorations. Chairs, tables, umbrellas, and other outdoor items can easily be lifted and thrown by strong winds, posing a significant danger to people and property. It is crucial to secure these items or move them indoors before a hurricane approaches.

Storing patio furniture and decorations in a secure location, such as a garage or storage unit, can prevent them from becoming hazardous projectiles during a storm.

Trash and Recycling Bins

Another often overlooked item that can transform into a dangerous projectile during a hurricane is the humble trash and recycling bin. These seemingly innocuous objects can be easily moved by strong winds, causing damage to buildings, vehicles, and even individuals in their path.

To prevent this, make sure to securely anchor your trash and recycling bins to the ground or bring them indoors ahead of a hurricane. This small precaution can go a long way in safeguarding your community from unnecessary risks.

Building Materials and Construction Debris

In association-governed communities, construction and maintenance projects may be underway, resulting in the presence of building materials and debris.

During a hurricane, loose boards, nails, shingles, and other construction materials can turn into dangerous projectiles if not properly secured. It is crucial to ensure that all construction sites are properly maintained and that any loose materials are promptly removed or adequately secured. This will help prevent potential accidents and injuries during severe weather conditions.

    Enhancing Curb Appeal

    First impressions are crucial, and the outside appeal of your property establishes the tone for prospective buyers. By selectively thinning tree canopies or removing obstructive branches, you can showcase these features more effectively, enhancing the overall attractiveness and functionality of your outdoor spaces.

    Promoting Safety and Accessibility

    The safety of your property is essential not only for your own peace of mind but also for enhancing its overall value. Residential tree lopping plays a critical role in achieving these objectives by addressing potential hazards and improving usability in the following ways:

    Hazard Mitigation

    Trees with overgrown or damaged branches pose significant safety hazards, especially during cyclones or high winds. Residential tree lopping involves the strategic removal of these hazards, reducing the likelihood of branches falling and causing damage to structures, vehicles, or people on your property. This proactive approach minimises potential liabilities and insurance risks, making your property more attractive to potential buyers concerned about safety.

In-depth damage assessment could not be completed in the first 12 hours following the earthquake. The City was unable to conduct a thorough damage assessment until first light on the morning of October 19. The Office of Public Works (OPW) dispatched City and volunteer building inspectors into the field and had primary responsibility for the City's overall damage assessment.

At the time of the earthquake, the three Office of General Services (OGS) chief building engineers were still in the field. They proceeded to do a visual damage assessment of all City-owned buildings. This was completed before dark. More detailed assessments waited until dawn when there was better light and the OPW building inspectors were able to join the OGS building engineers.

Three facilities which received immediate attention were City Hall, City Hall West, and the City's Municipal Service Center. City Hall and City Hall West housed the majority of the City's departments. Both suffered significant structural and non-structural damage. Although the quake occurred after most employees had gone home, it was still important to check both these buildings for injured employees who may have been left behind in the initial evacuation. This was of particular concern in City departments how to conduct a damage assessment and when to resume normal operations.

B. Building Inspections

At 6:00 a.m. on October 18th, Office of Public Works (OPW) Engineering and Design Services Division began to assess the damage as well as to track and record all reports. -- Accuracy of these records provided documentation for State and Federal aid requests. This was the first concerted effort by the City to track incoming damage reports.

Prior to the earthquake some of the Design Services staff had been through the- Applied Technology Council's (ATC) training on procedures for conducting building inspections following an earthquake. They trained building inspectors who were sent into the field. OPW, Construction and Field Services developed an inspection process from the ATC manuals, using the ATC-20 format. This was taught in an abbreviated form to City employees and volunteers doing inspections. Additional inspectors were solicited from surrounding cities and counties. Staff also used personal contacts to recruit more inspectors.

By carefully selecting positions that offer a balance of visibility and protection, sniper teams can optimize their effectiveness while minimizing the risk of detection. Additionally, the natural features of hills and valleys can serve as effective barriers against enemy advances, providing snipers with strategic advantages in engaging targets from a position of strength.

Strategic Use of Man-Made Structures for Concealment

Strategic Use of Man-Made Structures for Concealment involves leveraging existing buildings, walls, and structures to mask a sniper team’s presence and activities. Urban environments offer an array of opportunities for concealment, using structures like abandoned buildings or rooftops to remain unseen while maintaining a strategic vantage point.

Additionally, man-made structures such as vehicles or debris can be strategically positioned to create artificial barriers, providing both cover and a hidden position for snipers. Integrating into the surroundings is crucial, as blending with the architecture or environment helps snipers evade detection and maintain a tactical advantage.

By utilizing windows, doors, and other openings in buildings, sniper teams can observe and engage targets discreetly while minimizing their own exposure. Effective communication and coordination within the team is essential to make the most of man-made structures for concealment, ensuring seamless operations and successful mission outcomes.

Camouflage Techniques for Effective Cover

Camouflage techniques play a crucial role in providing effective cover for sniper operations. Ghillie suits are a staple in concealing snipers within their surroundings, utilizing natural elements to blend seamlessly into the environment. These specialized suits break the human outline and mimic the textures and colors of the surrounding terrain, enhancing the sniper’s ability to remain undetected.

Additionally, face paint and visual disruption techniques are utilized to further conceal the sniper’s identity. By applying face paint in strategic patterns and utilizing disruptive elements, such as stripes or patterns, snipers create optical illusions that help break up their silhouette, making it harder for enemies to spot them. This meticulous attention to detail in camouflage enhances the effectiveness of the sniper’s cover.

Moreover, the selection of appropriate camouflage techniques depends on the specific environment and terrain in which the sniper operates. 2023 Trends In Fenestration Industry

23rd December 2022

The fenestration industry, which includes the manufacturing and installation of windows, doors, and other openings in buildings, is constantly evolving and adapting to new trends and technologies. Here are a few trends that we can expect to see in the fenestration industry in 2023.

Increased focus on energy efficiency

As the demand for energy-efficient buildings continues to grow, we can expect to see an increase in the use of energy-efficient windows and doors in new construction projects. This includes the use of double and triple glazing and insulating frames to help reduce energy loss and improve the overall energy efficiency of a building.

Greater use of smart technology

Smart windows, doors and blinds that can be controlled and monitored remotely through a smartphone or tablet are becoming increasingly popular. These advanced products allow homeowners to control their windows and doors remotely, as well as track their energy usage and adjust settings to optimise energy efficiency.

Growing popularity of sliding doors

Sliding doors, which can be used to connect indoor and outdoor spaces, are becoming increasingly popular in both residential and commercial buildings. I. Introduction

Droughts are hydro-meteorological events affecting vast regions and causing significant structural and non-structural damages. Drought predictions may prevent these adverse consequences to a significant extent. In order to reach such a target, it is necessary to develop a method of monitoring based on the available past experiences as well as on environmental conditions.

Figure 1: Location map of the Tel watershed, Odisha

There are several indices that measure to what extent precipitation for a given period has deviated from historically established norms. Although none of the major indices is inherently superior to the rest in all circumstances, some indices are better suited than others for certain uses. The Standardized Precipitation Index (SPI) was designed to quantify the precipitation deficit for multiple time scales, which reflect the impact of drought on the availability of different water resources. Soil moisture conditions respond to precipitation anomalies on a relatively short time scale, while groundwater, stream flow, and reservoir storage reflect the longer-term precipitation anomalies as in [12]. For these reasons, McKee et al. [2] originally calculated the SPI for 3-, 6-, 12-, 24-, and 48-month moving average time scales. als and Gaskets

EPDM rubber seals and gaskets are widely used in various industries due to their excellent properties. Here’s a breakdown of their key characteristics and applications:

  1. Weather Resistance: EPDM rubber exhibits exceptional resistance to weathering, ozone, and UV exposure, making it suitable for outdoor applications. It doesn’t degrade easily under sunlight or harsh weather conditions, making it ideal for seals and gaskets in automotive, construction, and marine industries.
  2. Temperature Resistance: EPDM can withstand a wide range of temperatures, from -50°C to 150°C (-58°F to 302°F), without losing its elasticity or mechanical properties. This thermal stability makes it suitable for both hot and cold environments, such as automotive cooling systems or HVAC systems.
  3. Chemical Resistance: EPDM is resistant to a variety of chemicals, including acids, alkalis, and polar solvents. This makes it suitable for use in applications where exposure to different chemicals is common, such as in chemical processing plants or laboratories.
  4. Water Resistance: EPDM Gaskets has excellent water resistance properties, which make it ideal for use in sealing applications where protection against moisture ingress is essential. It’s commonly used in sealing windows, doors, and other openings in buildings, as well as in plumbing systems.
  5. Flexibility and Elasticity: EPDM rubber is highly flexible and elastic, allowing it to conform to irregular surfaces and maintain a tight seal over time. This flexibility also makes it resistant to cracking or splitting, even after prolonged use or exposure to extreme temperatures.
  6. Electrical Insulation: EPDM rubber has good electrical insulation properties, making it suitable for use in electrical enclosures, cable seals, and other applications where electrical conductivity needs to be minimized.
  7. Low Gas Permeability: EPDM rubber has low gas permeability, which makes it suitable for use in sealing applications where gas or vapor leakage needs to be prevented, such as in automotive fuel systems or HVAC ductwork.

About: EPDM rubber seals and gaskets offer a combination of weather resistance, temperature resistance, chemical resistance, and flexibility, making them versatile and reliable for a wide range of sealing applications across various industries.
